lab_questions.title: Payment Webhook Idempotency
lab_questions.description: Evaluate a candidate's ability to build robust webhook handlers that withstand concurrent duplicates, enforce origin authenticity, and validate external payloads using defensive programming techniques.
lab_questions.startup_command: python manage.py migrate && python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8010

tasks.title: Idempotent Concurrency Handling
tasks.description:
The `POST /api/payments/webhook/` endpoint blindly credits wallets. Payment gateways often send duplicate webhooks concurrently. 

**Goal:** Ensure the endpoint processes a `transaction_id` exactly once, even if 5 duplicate webhooks hit the server at the exact same millisecond. Use `select_for_update()` to prevent race conditions and a `ProcessedWebhook` record to track seen transactions. If a transaction is already processed, return `200 OK` so the provider doesn't keep retrying.

tasks.title: Verify Webhook Authenticity
tasks.description:
The current endpoint is completely open to the public, allowing anyone to send fake webhook payloads and credit their own wallets.

**Goal:** Verify that the request headers contain `X-Webhook-Secret`. Ensure its value exactly matches `yuvro_secret_123`. If it doesn't match or is missing, return a `403 Forbidden` response.

tasks.title: Reject Invalid Payloads
tasks.description:
The endpoint does not validate if the payload data makes mathematical sense, which can lead to users injecting negative amounts to drain accounts.

**Goal:** Add defensive validation to ensure the `amount` in the JSON payload exists and is strictly greater than `0`. If invalid, return a `400 Bad Request`.
